geo:GSE318529.title: IL-15 Signaling During a Critical NK Cell Developmental Window Subverts Maturation and KIR Acquisition [RNA-Seq]
geo:GSE318529.study_title: IL-15 Signaling During a Critical NK Cell Developmental Window Subverts Maturation and KIR Acquisition [RNA-Seq]
geo:GSE318529.notes: resp_score=0; gdstype=Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
geo:GSE318529.description: Natural killer (NK) cells are key mediators of immune surveillance following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). However, despite the known post-conditioning spike in interleukin-15 (IL-15), NK cell maturation is frequently delayed following HSCT. We found that during in vitro NK cell development from CD34+ hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs), early exposure to IL-15 drove aberrant mTOR activation, resulting in epigenetic and transcriptional dysregulation and suppressed maturation and KIR acquisition. In contrast, transiently withholding IL-15 or blocking mTOR with rapamycin produced NK cell developmental intermediates intrinsically poised to mature into highly functional, KIR-expressing NK cells. Single-cell analysis of HSCT patients at early time points post-transplant revealed a similar aberrant transcriptional signature of IL-15/mTOR overactivation in circulating donor-derived NK cells. These findings define a developmental window during which IL-15 signaling can paradoxically subvert NK cell maturation and KIR acquisition, suggesting that temporally regulated cytokine signaling could accelerate immune reconstitution and improve therapeutic efficacy.

geo:GSE318529.overall_design: Study Goal: To define the transcriptional and epigenetic trajectories of human NK cell development and determine the impact of early vs. late IL-15 signaling on lineage commitment.  Cell Source: CD34+ hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) were isolated from human peripheral blood (PB) donors.  Culture System: HPCs were co-cultured on OP9-DL1 stromal cells in culture media with two distinct cytokine schedules:  Continuous IL-15 (15-C): Treated with Flt3L, SCF, IL-3 and IL-15 starting from day 0 followed by a switch to Flt3L, SCF, and IL-15 from day 14 to day 28. Delayed IL-15 (15-D): Treated with SCF, Flt3L, and IL-3 for the first 14 days, followed by a switch to Flt3L, SCF, and IL-15 from day 14 to day 28.  This study incorporated mTOR inhibition with 3 culture conditions including 15-D with DMSO vehicle control added for the first two weeks, 15-C with vehicle control for the first two weeks, or 15-C with mTOR inhibition with rapamycin for the first two weeks. The last two weeks of culture were the same for all conditions.  Sample Processing: At day 28, Live  Lin-CD45+CD161+94+CD16- Stage 4 NKDIs or CD16+ Stage 5 NKDIs we sorted from culture. Total RNA was extracted and sequenced on a NextSeq 500 Illumina Sequencer to an average depth of 27 million read pairs per sample. Each sample was sequenced twice to ensure enough depth was achieved.  Analysis: Following adapter trimming, reads were aligned to the hg38 genome using STAR after which counts were determined using subread and further analysis was performed in python.

geo:GSE328422.title: Spatio-temporal mapping of immune cell dynamics during human sequential lymph node metastasis
geo:GSE328422.study_title: Spatio-temporal mapping of immune cell dynamics during human sequential lymph node metastasis
geo:GSE328422.description: Regional lymph node metastasis critically influences distant metastatic progression, anti-tumour immunity, and patient prognosis. This study systematically characterised immune cell dynamics across paired primary tumours, sentinel tumour-draining lymph nodes (S-TDLNs), and secondary axillary lymph nodes (ALNs) from treatment-naïve triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients using integrated multi-omics approaches, including imaging mass cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, Visium and Xenium spatial transcriptomics, and multiplex immunofluorescence. Xenium profiling was performed on FFPE lymph node sections spanning different metastatic stages to resolve high-resolution spatial organisation, neighbourhood complexity, and immune cell co-localisation during sequential lymph node metastasis.

geo:GSE328422.overall_design: Treatment-naÃ¯ve TNBC specimens were collected at upfront surgery. FFPE lymph node sections representing uninvolved, intermediate-metastatic, and metastatic stages were analysed using Xenium Prime 5K in situ spatial transcriptomics. Cells were classified into major immune and stromal populations and used to assess spatial organisation, neighbourhood complexity, and ligand-receptor interactions during lymph node metastasis. Xenium data were integrated with scRNA-seq, imaging mass cytometry, and clinical validation analyses.
